chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The woman tatooist and the tattooed woman, and the one who raises the price (at an auction) without intending to buy it, and the one who is pleased with that, are accursed ones upon the tongue of Muhammad (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.وَالنَّاجِشُ: And the one who raises the price (auctioneer)
key_terms.وَالْمَنْجُوشُ: And the one who is pleased with the price raising

ai.seo_question: Who are the four people cursed by the Prophet Muhammad according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi identifies four categories of individuals cursed by the Prophet, specifically highlighting the washer and the washed (tattooing), as well as the munajish (one who bids falsely to inflate prices). In Shia jurisprudence, this curse underscores the prohibition of gharar (uncertainty/deception) in trade and the alteration of Allah's creation, linking ritual purity concerns with commercial ethics.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The woman tatooist and the tattooed woman, and the one who raises the price (at an auction) without intending to buy it, and the one who is pleased with that, are accursed ones upon the tongue of Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 13. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has condemned tattooing persons and those who are tattooed, those who raise the price of a piece of goods for sale without the intention to buy and those who agree to such act.’”
